reviews.comment: The class itself is hit-or-miss, but Professor Fullerton is somewhat accessible outside of lecture. Homework can be tough, but the class is curved. Consider using study tools like Unstuck study alongside the textbook to stay on top of the material.

If you don't know how to code don't take him as your prof, I didn't and he doesn't really teach you how to code he just goes through the slideshow. His grading is a bit weird so don't stress if you do bad on the midterm and final just focus on doing good on the zybooks and & quizzes, he drops one thing in each category so it should help out a lot!

His lectures were very rushed, much of which was due to there being too much content for the allotted class time. However, he finished nearly every class early which wasn't good in this case because he would skip through almost all of the slides during the lecture. Be prepared to learn the content through other sources.

About the class: 216 isn't great. They made the final easier this year, but they might make it hard again next year. Labs are annoying but not prof-dependent, rather TA dependent. 

About the prof: Attendance was optional until the last 2 weeks. He generously curves the final. He seems like a caring guy. 

Take this class with friends if possible.

The labs themselves are fine and usually easy to get good grades on, but the lecture part of this class isn't the best. It's not 100% his fault, as he usually has to cover 50-70 slides in 50 minutes so he just clicks through, but he's a bit condescending and takes FOREVER to grade HW, and the HW is usually hard. The class is at least curved though.

Professor Fullerton was OK, but it just felt like he had little interest in teaching the class. Mostly optional lectures (where he clicked through slides) and fairly tough homework and homework quizzes. Critical and a little condescending during office hours.
dont take him.

He was mid and very accessible outside of class. He sends emails if participation is required in class, but otherwise, I skipped his lectures. If I could describe him and his class, it would be mid. Take him, he is overall nice guy.

A lazy professor who is also overly passive aggressive. Uses notes and homework from other profs. Would make us turn in all our homework assignments twice, one including our work and one as a Canvas quiz, so if you got something wrong you would get penalized twice. Homework also has no feedback.

He was fairly nice until the end of the semester. His lecture style is to get through the slides as soon as possible, but that causes him to skip many slides. Make sure that you go back and review them to get all of the information. There is not much feedback on the HW. Lab depends on TAs.

I understand 216 has lots of students, but compared to what other professors do I would just describe his teaching style and effort this semester as lazy. Nothing else. He went through the slides in 30 minutes so everyone could leave class early. He didnt even bother to give feedback on any hw assignment and had us submit a quiz for canvas.

Engr/phys 216 has a terrible class set up in general with one 50 minute class per week, but Dr. Fullerton is definitely more difficult compared to other professors who teach it. Many other professors offer grade boosts that he does not. He is very blunt in emails/office hours, which makes you feel stupid. Overall okay guy, but I wish he was nicer.

Decent professor, but not the best lecturer. He reads off the slides. However, it seems that he is trying to mention some important information. It feels like the slides are just too long for a 50-minute lecture once every week. Homework is difficult but I think that is intended to sort of do well on the finals. The finals didn't feel too bad.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 216 is probably the hardest class out there for freshman engineers, which is mainly due to the final exam being designed to fail you. However, Fullerton did try his best with the time that he could, as 50 min per week isn't nearly enough time to cover all of the content in this course. He does give a lot of homework, but no more than other classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He cannot lecture and when you ask him questions he responds condescendingly, he expects you to know the material even with his lack of effective lecturing. He is way tougher than other profs. Grades only on accuracy with little to no feedback. No check answers quizzes, no points back on the midterm, etc. Makes the class harder than needed.

His lectures are very boring, and you don't need him to understand the material. He can be condescending at times, and that gets really annoying. His homeworks are harder than the other classes, but attendance isn't mandatory.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 216 just sucks in general. Dr. Fullerton is given like 50 slides of content to teach in 50 minutes. Dr. Fullerton gives much harder homework, and expects extra work like FBDs, but that's to ensure understanding and get you ready for the final. Also, Dr. Fullerton doesn't allow corrections, but that's to give a bigger curve after finals.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Felt very condescending. When I went to his office hours he seemed like he wanted to get rid of me as fast as possible. He had 50mins each class to get through 50 slides, but most of the time he would just talk through 15 slides with no examples, then say "that's kind of it" and end class in 20 minutes without actually TEACHING THE MATERIAL. AVOID.
Extremely difficult homework relative to all the other professors, and seems to get actually mad when you go to office hours to ask. Avoid at all costs lol
Bumahh Professor do not take for engr216

annoying, man splains, does not help with hw at all even in office hours. comparatively much harder than the other 216 professors, ex: no midterm retakes, no margin of error or very little for hws. If you don't care about your grade, feel free to join the class
Terrible professor, assigns absurd amounts of homework, and incredibly condescending. Do everything in your power to not take this man

Don't know why, but I really liked this guy. He's clearly very intelligent and articulate. Everything he does wrong is a product of his circumstances. He has to go through a ton of material in 50 min and this is his first year teaching the class. The grades are low, but he has said he will curve. Overall nice and smart professor.

One of the worst professors I've had, and I've taken a class with Janet Blumel. He assigns so much more work than other profs, on the midterm, and hw most other professors gave the students a free 100, however, Fullerton had to go out of his way to make our lives miserable.  He's a terrible lecturer and condescending when answering questions.

Terrible class, bad professor. He is sarcastic and condescending. He gives an insane amount of homework compared to other professors for this class and doesn't grade it; he put up a quiz where you input your answers, and there's no partial credit and margins of error are very narrow, so the scores are low. I would have avoided him if I could have.

This class just sucks and Fullerton did what he could. He doesnt grade the assignments, its the TA. The homework answer quizzes are always an F grade. Hes given 50+ slides to read in 50min. Go to his office hours and build a relationship, that will help. Be respectful. He is easy to talk to when you're not only wanting to submit a late assignment.

Genuinely a horrible professor for an already horrible class, would give homework answer quizzes because he couldn't be bothered to actually grade with feedback, so it was often extremely difficult to figure out what you were doing wrong. He also got very angry if you ever went to office hours to ask a question. The worst professor I've had so far.

Lectures are him going through 50+ slides of complicated subjects. hw is very hard and long, uses dr. o hw and notes. Can't see answers for hw quizzes he uses to grade hw, so u have no idea what ur doing wrong. lectures notes don't help much as hw is very different. worst class i've taken this semester. labs are a lot of work but they're free a's.

He basically just went through a slideshow and read off of it. If you don't know how to code I wouldn't recommend him. How well you do in the class depends on what group you choose the first week. He was a little too chill but his TA's are amazing and they help you a lot. I would do the other assigments on zybooks if you have never coded.

Without coding experience, this class will be hard. He reads slides for the most part and works through some examples. A positive is that he seems as eager to get out of class as the students are. He is easy to reach by email. He grades fairly. He seems a little cynical at times. An overall average professor.

Super chill and funny. He has a very laid back style so it's up to you to finish your work. Did not lecture extensively, but he posts the powerpoints so they are very helpful to look back on. It's a hard class if you do not already have coding experience, but he is very understanding and is willing to help.

You work on coding assignments with 3 other group members. Exams are moderately difficult if you haven't had a coding class before. He doesn't make you do the zybook activities which are required for some other professors.

Fullerton wasnt really that bad of a professor, just frustrating that i learned that his in class quizzes and labs were much harder than other professors. Exams are designed to be confusing and will most definitely tank your grade. Overall he was pretty approachable, but I think i just had bad luck when it came to grading from the ta's.

Good prof, very nice. ENGR102 is just a lot of work no matter the prof. His lectures are simple and to the point but I had to do a lot of learning on my own time. I struggled to keep up with the amount of work that was assigned. Pick good group members who can code because they will make or break your grade.

Pretty chill guy outside of class, even at 8am. Kinda funny, overall decent at explaining things. 

A lot of the struggle of ENGR 102 is just the overall class, which is streamlined by the department. So you can't really hit him on the difficulty. Exams are tough, quizzes are hit or miss. 

Not a bad professor, consider taking him

Dr. Fullerton is super chill and is super lenient when it comes to class. Attendance is optional except for the 15-minute quizzes at the start of class each week. He gives very brief lectures each week and doesn't require any of the time-consuming practice assignments that most of the other profs require. Highly recommend taking him if possible.
Easy class for those who have taken computer science in high school. He only requires you to do the labs, which is a huge time saver. Cool professor.

Professor Fullerton is a solid choice but the course is difficult at best for non-computer programming majors. Labs are one of the biggest parts of the course and are extremely time-consuming. I highly recommend going back and rewatching posted lectures when you get stuck on the labs. Professor is very helpful with lab group issues.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Labs weren't too hard. Professor was pretty chill. Exams were tough so try to do well on the labs and quizzes

Unless you're an absolute beginner, you won't really learn much coding. Professor and his TAs are pretty helpful. All the assignments and quizzes are very straightforward. Exams are hard, so make up for them by making sure you don't miss any assignments or quizzes.

He's a pretty good professor. I see a of of people saying he gets irritated when asked a question. The questions people asked in my class were always things he had literally gone over just a few seconds ago, I would have been pretty annoyed too. He does a good job of explaining the labs and definitely knows what has talking about.

He is a very laidback professor. The labs werent terribly hard. He assigned groups parts of the lab, but he was cool about changing groups if you felt like you did all the work. I got two Bs and the rest were all As on my labs BUT the tests brought me to a B in the class. I felt like the practice he gave out for the exam didnt really help me.

Dr. Fullerton was a pretty good professor, but I found that most times I didn't really have to go to class. The labs and tests are pretty hard, but that's not really his fault. I don't really think he likes freshmen, so only ask good questions and read your emails. My biggest piece of advice is to find a study group in the same section as you.

Fullerton's ok. He's really laid back, but if you ask him a question, he tends to get irritated without actually giving a helpful answer. It's nice that he doesn't make you use the zybook, which means less homework, but he really just doesn't seem to care about the class, and didn't provide much useful feedback for anything. Pretty easy A though.

ENGR 102 with professor Fullerton is a breeze. Even if you have no prior programming experience, his biweekly lectures show exactly how to do the labs. Otherwise, if you know what youre doing, the lectures are completely optional. The exams are gonna take a moderate amount of studying but overall not impossible to make an A on.
Didnt really care if you attended class but wasnt very approachable. Had a temper and sometimes didnt like to answer questions. Gave out few study materials for exams

He, is a decent teacher. What makes the class hard, is that the labs are not at all something that someone who has never done coding can just bang out. It takes so so much time. Having Fullerton makes the class easier as he opted to not have one of the harder labs that other classes had, aswell as not give us a final project.

Extremely chill professor. Made the zybook optional while other classes had to read/do the activities for a grade. Decided not to have a final project which was a major pain for other classes. Class was not mandatory. Labs are pretty self explanatory. Easier than high school computer science classes. Take him if you already know basic programming.

Dr. Fullerton is a funny guy. His class doesn't really need many lectures, but he is very relaxed when it comes to attendance. If you want less work and more useful lessons than other professors, take him. He doesn't follow useless and unnecessary requirements, he just teaches what he thinks you will actually use in the future!

Prof Fullerton is such a funny guy. He's super ready and able to help so long as you're respectful and don't interrupt him. Great dude! I loved this class because of him :) It's also easy as heck if you've taken coding classes before.

He's nice but can be mean in a friendly way, just don't ask him the same question twice. He's very chill about attendance and always says if you have something better to do, you can leave and watch the recording later. We only get graded on our weekly content quizzes and two coding labs. If you've taken ComSci in Highschool this will be a breeze.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fullerton does a great gob at explaining ways to do the labs though pictures and lectures. He does not like the textbook or the department quizzes and does not use/do them. (No textbook / No quizzes) If you are a first time coder take him because he explains it very well. He does have a bit of a temper, and does not like to repeat himself.

I was a bit worried when I saw I got Dr. Fullerton after seeing previous reviews. However I couldn't be more glad I got him as a professor. He is one of the only profs that doesn't require zybook, and did demos for every lab so you knew what you were doing. Brush up on python a bit before taking the course and you'll do great.

Did not help much throughout the COVID-19 pandemic when classes were transferred to online. Falsely accused me of cheating on exams by using other students for help. Didnt even lecture throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, just let the students figure it out themselves.

He skimmed over lecture slides (thank god), and answered questions thoroughly. He is flexible with quizzes and gives an extra day to specific topics if enough students say they are having trouble. Whenever I asked Fullerton questions, it always seemed like he was annoyed with something. Labs are not hard, but exams can be a surprise sometimes.

Having programming experience from high school helped a lot because he would explain things but it felt like he expected everyone to know the subject already. Tests are tough, but that's engineering for you.

He's not a great lecturer and he was kind of rude at times when people asked him questions. I personally didn't like him as a professor because he didn't teach the material well and was sometimes rude, but what I did like about him was that he would postpone quizzes sometimes if he knew we felt uncomfortable with the material. Go to SI sessions.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Fullerton doesn't seem like the most approachable professor but he's really nice and will randomly just decide to not have quizzes. As long as you do the labs and understand what's going on, you'll be fine in class. You need to show up for participation but you don't have to pay attention! He's great.

I skipped class whenever there wasn't a quiz because he talks for so damn long. Attendance not needed if you have prior coding experience. Labs are time consuming, but not too difficult (group lab mileage may vary). Quizzes were free 100s. Tests are more difficult, but if you do very good on labs + quiz and decent on tests you should get an A.

Dr. Fullerton is a very no-nonsense professor. He prefers to get students working as soon as possible instead of lecturing. There are group projects every week, but they're easily manageable. However, do NOT underestimate the tests. Even though the class seems easy, make sure to study up on Python syntax before quizzes and exams.

Great professor in terms of teaching. He has a bit of a temper so ask him reasonable questions. His TA's grade his quizzes and exams so if you see any mistakes on your graded exams contact them. He doesn't require zybook but recommends it. Pushes quizzes back to learn the harder topics. if you put in effort, you'll love him, easy A/B .

He will make sure you understand the material. Pushes back quizzes and due dates to spend more time on harder topics. Textbook is optional. Doesn't take attendance but if you don't show up, you won't learn/you'll miss a quiz and get a 0. Thoroughly explains concepts to make sure the class understands the topics.

This professor is so rude to people who try to ask him for regrading the exams. Guys, exams are heavy and it really can change your gpa. You don't want this professor's assistants (students) to grade your exam without grading it carefully. By all means, do not take his class!!!!

Dr. Fullerton cares a lot about his students, he constantly pushed back quizzes and assignments (sometimes made them optional) so that he could explain the topic further and go over what was confusing. He understands lectures are boring, and does the best he can to make them easier. Still, coding is hard so hope that you're in a good group!
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fullerton is unintentionally the most interesting prof I have this semester. If you take him for ENGR 102, and you sort of know what you're doing, you'll be fine. This class is fairly easy, but beware that the tests are on paper and he doesn't grade them, the TA's do.

Not as great for ENGR102. I had no Python experience and it seems like Fullerton HATES teaching. He posts the slides online but the labs are much more complicated than the basic slides. The midterm and final are pretty rough but the labs count for a greater percentage of your grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Tracy is a fantastic professor! If you can, make sure to take him! He can be a little snappy however- he gets upset if you ask him a question that is already answered on the assignment sheet.

So Prof. Fullerton is a great and nice guy, he expects some work out of you, but is understanding that we are Freshamn first semester as well. Other sections must use the ZyBook to learn Python, but he doesn't require us to so I didn't waste the money. Highly recommend him, because if you put in effore, you'll love him, overall an easy A/B
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Over all probably one of the best engr112 profs you can get. He actually took time on class to deeply explain topics that were eventually tested over. Only negatives are him being a tough grader especially on projects and him having a little bit of a temper. Most of the time hes funny and nice and has no problem extending dates and/or ending class
Fullerton is a great guy who makes his class enjoyable. Just do what he asks and you should be fine in the class.

Fullerton is by far one of the greatest professors I've had thus far my freshman year. He's funny, cares about his students, and is very dedicated to his job. His peer teachers grade, so depending on them is how hard they grade. I came in with no programming experience which made the class a little harder for me but still enjoyable nonetheless
Great Professor! Had him for Engr 111 and 112 and I would highly recommend taking him for both! He is easy and doesn't give much homework.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: TLF was a very solid professor. He made such a boring class fun and did not really give much homework compared to the other profs. When it comes to grading, he is on the more difficult side, but his expectations are clear. His lectures are very engaging and concise, so you make sure you attend class. He is probably the best 111 +112 prof there is.

ENGR 111-- Dr. Fullerton was always friendly and cared about his students. He never went onto a new topic until he was sure that all the students knew the material. Very easy class if you do the work (not too much work at all). ENGR 111 is boring and useless in general, but he did a good job with it.

Dr. Fullerton is brutally honest when it comes to teaching. If he doesn't want to give an assignment or talk about a topic, then will say so. He is very knowledgeable when it comes to engineering. The exams can be stressful if you under-study. The Lego robot group projects are stressful no matter what.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Fullerton is a very chill professor. His walks you through all the assignments and makes them super easy to complete. When learning MATLAB, we never really had any quizzes whereas other classes did. He makes clear what you need to do to be successful in his class. You are ranked by performance on the Lego projects at the end of the semester.

This professor is awesome! He is funny and very well respected by me. When told to read the ZyBook chapters, actually do it and you will smooth sail through this class. This was the easiest class my Freshman year and I would highly recommend taking this professor.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: ENGR 111 is going away soon, but he would be a great prof for any course. His lectures are entertaining, and he cracks lots of jokes. He wanted to make sure we got good at planning before we started to write code which was pretty smart. I would take him again for any course if I had the chance. Easy tests, barely any homework!

Fullerton's a real chill dude, he kinda doesn't seem like he doesn't know what's going on with the 112 curriculum(especially matlab), but that translates to his exams being pretty easy.  He did teach an intro to statics fairly well and he cuts out a lot of the unnecessary nonsense of 112.  But best of all he really guides you on your big project.

Fullerton is one of the more solid intorductory engineering professors. While he gives homework more often than other teachers, he doesn't grade too tough on it and he does it to make sure students understand the material enough for exams. Not too great with advice regarding social stuff (meaning group project problems). I recommend him.

Fullerton is a great professor. The grading is clear and understanding. He explains what needs to be on the assignment and when it is due. Due dates in this class can be messed with depending on what was going on. Go to lecture and do well.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: TAKE TRACY. He's the bomb. He will not give you quizzes over common material that he doesn't like or agree with. He's great at lectures usually but sometimes the common ENGR 111 material is boring. He doesn't give that much homework and doesn't pick up in class activities. He has a temper sometimes and usually isn't the best with questions though.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He's awesome idk why he teaches engr 111 and 112 a lot instead of upper level classes

Fullerton is the man. He knows the material, is very good at answering questions, and doesn't try to kill you with homework. When given an assignment, he is very specific on what he wants to be done. Grading depends on the T.A.'s, but Fullerton does tell them to be easy and what not. Very recommended.
He is such a great professor I asked to be forced into his 112 class for next semester. He cares about you and your understanding of the concepts, even the stupid ones TAMU forces.

I wish I could take his class next semester, but it's entirely full. Very good professor, lectures were interesting enough to pay attention to. Only real complaint is group projects, but I believe those are more TAMU's fault than Fullerton's.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Tracy is the best professor ever. He makes his ENGR111 class as fun as it can be. Regardless of who your professor is, ENGR111 is a waste of time and you will inevitably be assigned group projects. With the TLF however, his sassiness and humor at least make the class slightly entertaining.

Tracy Leo Fullerton is my hero. He gave up his fancy mechanical engineering job to teach freshmen how to hook up Legos, so he is understandably sassy. His ENGR111 class is pretty easy if you're not an idiot (and he'll help you determine if you are). He has a very clear way of doing things, and is super pragmatic. He's a pretty fly dude.

Always gives time to ask questions at the beginning of class before RATs, goes out of his way to make sure students understand the concepts, even slowed down the matlab portion of class to make sure everyone actually knew what was going on. Would definitely recommend
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Fullerton was the chillest prof I had this semester. He made class fun and really easy
The TLF is amazing. He is honestly a great professor and does not assign a lot of homework. He is respected by his students and respects them as future engineers.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Fullerton wants you to succeed. He also wanted us to do the important aspects from the class and had less work that was busy work and more of the pertinent information. He knows exactly what he is doing, is flexible with the class, and puts in his effort to help you learn what needs to be learned.

Dr Fullerton has very clear lectures and is a helpful professor. Not a big fan of partial credit on exams. It is expected that you have a semester long group project similar to ENGR 111. Know how your project works or he will chew you out on it and it is embarrassing. He does get rowdy sometimes, but overall a good 112 prof.

Dr. Tracy was very good at lecturing HOWEVER beware his temper. He flew off the handle on multiple occasions, almost always made students feel stupid in front of the class after they asked questions on the material, and was generally rude. I don't recommend taking him unless anxiety helps you.

Wow, I really felt like I learned things in this class.  Overall, the course was hard because of all the time spent on group projects and homework, but it was doable.  As for Fullerton himself, he wasn't too bad.... gave some powerful lectures and offered help when I'd ask for it.  He's a relatively tough grader, so watch out for that.

Dr. Fullerton likes to do things his own way, and has a pretty good way of doing things! He is very clear in lecture and always takes feedback from his students to ensure they are understanding the material. He writes his own tests and emails students with regular updates. Only issue is a too short time limit on exams. Take Fullerton if you can!

Dr. Fullerton takes pride in doing things his way and believing that as the correct way. His lectures are clear, and he consistently takes feedback from the students to make sure they are understanding the material. He writes all of his own tests. Only issue is there is too little time given on all of his tests, work fast! TAKE FULLERTON FOR ENGR!

Tracy is a great guy, who really wants you to do well in his class. No matter what this is a tough class, especially with groups and the projects. More the most part he will try to help you out as much as possible. Probably one of the better choices for this class.
Robot project takes up a lot of your time. He moves due dates around constantly, but keeps the course on track.  Lecture slides are posted and he lectures well.

Fullerton keeps his lectures interesting and answers any and all questions. There are 3 group projects during the semester that you will work on with your assigned team that aren't too difficult, just very time consuming. Make sure you watch every single module as you will be tested on them at the beginning and end of classes.
